events.title: Rusthold, still lit
events.text: 'Rusthold's lights are still on,' says Ma, thin with distance. 'I checked. Nobody picks up. The tide comes out of the gates, not out of us, so it won't stop for being tired. The Kettle Yards went an hour after you left, and the Fenn rows after that. Keep moving. I'm parked by the exit beacon with the engines hot and a hold full of people who all want to talk. Come and say hello when you pass. I'd like to see the hull.'

choices.text: Tell her you'll stop by the barge.

outcomes.text: 'Good,' says Ma. 'Bring your own mug.' The line clicks, and for a minute the cabin is quieter than it was.

choices.text: Ask her to keep the tea warm.

outcomes.text: 'It's always warm,' says Ma, 'it's the one thing on this barge that is.' The line goes dead, and somebody on your crew has started to hum.

events.title: Lists and stamps
events.text: 'Concord is holding Meridian,' says Ma. 'Lists and stamps. If your name's on the list you get a berth. If it isn't, you get a form. They're very good at it. The tide eats slowest where there's paperwork, which I find insulting. The Clans are scattering, and some are raiding. I'll forgive the ones who only take fuel. The next safe harbour is wherever I'm parked, by the exit. Meridian's second best, and it's cleaner.'

events.title: Answering
events.text: 'The Lumen say the gates are answering,' says Ma. 'That's their word. I asked what the gates were being asked, and the nice one stopped humming. That was all I got. I'm not accusing anybody. I'm saying the humming stopped. Two more yards went quiet behind you. The tide moves faster than my engines, so I've started parking ahead of it. You'll find me by the exit, same as before. Eat something.'

events.title: On time
events.text: 'Somebody is playing the Halcyon loop on every channel,' says Ma, 'and it's perfect. That's how I know it isn't them. The real one starts late. Don't follow anything on time. If a voice offers you a berth for the whole crew, ask it what the cough sounds like. The tide has most of what's behind us. I counted eleven stations on my wall and then I stopped counting. The harbour's by the exit. It's always by the exit.'

events.title: The long middle
events.text: 'You're in the long middle now,' says Ma. 'The gate approaches are a few regions off. I can feel them in the barge's plates, a low hum like Rusthold on Snap night, except it doesn't go away. The tide's thinner here, which means we're closer to where it starts. I'm tired. The children have learnt to sleep through the alarms. Next harbour's by the exit. After that it's Halcyon or it's nothing, and I'd rather it were Halcyon.'

events.title: Orla
events.text: 'We lost Orla,' says Ma. 'The dockmaster. She stayed on the Rusthold to close the doors, and nobody argued, which is how I knew. That's the thing nobody says about the Hollow: it's polite. It lets you finish your sentence. There are only a few stations left between here and the Reach, and I've bought fuel at all of them. The barge is by the exit. Come by. I'd like someone to tell the children the soup is real.'

events.title: Last stretch
events.text: 'Last stretch,' says Ma. 'The Reach is out there, and I can hear the loop. Real this time, I think. It's late. The tide's right behind us and the barge is slower than I'd like, so if I fall behind, go on without me. No, don't argue, I've got a clipboard. If you're near the exit I'll be there. If you're not, I'm behind you. Whoever's in your hold, take them in first.'
